title: Γυνὴ καὶ θεράπαιναι
part: The Widow and Her Maidservants (Chambry 89 · Perry 55)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 89 (= Perry 55). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Γυνὴ χήρα φίλεργος θεραπαινίδας ἔχουσα, ταύτας εἰώθει νυκτὸς ἐπὶ τὰ ἔργα ἐγείρειν πρὸς ἀλεκτροφωνίαν.
sentences.tr: Gynē chēra philergos therapainidas echousa, tautas eiōthei nyktos epi ta erga egeirein pros alektrophōnian.
sentences.l: A widow, industrious, having maidservants, was accustomed to rouse them by night to their work at cockcrow.
sentences.i: A hard-working widow who kept maidservants used to rouse them in the night, at cockcrow, to their work.
sentences.n: νυκτός is a genitive of time within which, 'in the course of the night'. πρὸς ἀλεκτροφωνίαν — the cock's crow is the household's clock; there is no other. ταύτας resumes an object already named, a colloquial redundancy the Greek tolerates and English does not.

sentences.t: Αἱ δὲ συνεχῶς καταπονούμεναι ἔγνωσαν δεῖν τὸν ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας ἀλέκτορα ἀποπνίξαι· ἐκεῖνον γὰρ ᾤοντο τῶν κακῶν αἴτιον εἶναι νύκτωρ ἐγείροντα τὴν δέσποιναν.
sentences.tr: Hai de synechōs kataponoumenai egnōsan dein ton epi tēs oikias alektora apopnixai· ekeinon gar ōionto tōn kakōn aition einai nyktōr egeironta tēn despoinan.
sentences.l: And they, being worn down continually, judged that they must throttle the cock of the house; for they thought that he was the cause of their troubles, rousing the mistress by night.
sentences.i: Worn down by it day after day, they decided they had to throttle the household cock: they thought he was the cause of their troubles, since it was he who woke the mistress in the night.
sentences.n: ἔγνωσαν δεῖν — the same idiom the farmer used in fable 86, here in service of a much worse plan. τὸν ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας ἀλέκτορα, 'the cock in the house', i.e. the household's own bird — the same ἐπί + genitive that fable 87 uses of τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας σκεύη, the goods about the house. Their reasoning is exactly right and their conclusion fatal: the cock is the cause, and removing it does not remove the mistress.

sentences.t: Συνέβη δὲ αὐταῖς πραξάσαις τοῦτο χαλεπωτέροις τοῖς δεινοῖς περιπεσεῖν· ἡ γὰρ δέσποινα ἀγνοοῦσα τὴν τῶν ἀλεκτρυόνων ὥραν νυχιέστερον ἐπὶ τὸ ἔργον ἤγειρεν.
sentences.tr: Synebē de autais praxasais touto chalepōterois tois deinois peripesein· hē gar despoina agnoousa tēn tōn alektryonōn hōran nychiesteron epi to ergon ēgeiren.
sentences.l: But it befell them, having done this, to fall into harsher troubles; for the mistress, not knowing the hour of the cocks, roused them to the work at a more nightly hour.
sentences.i: But having done it, they fell into worse trouble than before: the mistress, with no way of knowing the hour the cocks crowed, now roused them to work deeper in the night.
sentences.n: συνέβη takes a dative and an infinitive, 'it happened to them to…'; αὐταῖς πραξάσαις folds the deed and its victims into one phrase. νυχιέστερον is a comparative adverb built on νύχιος, 'nightly' — an uncommon formation, 'at a more nocturnal hour'.

sentences.t: Οὕτω πολλοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ ἴδια βουλεύματα κακῶν αἴτια γίνεται.
sentences.tr: Houtō pollois anthrōpois ta idia bouleumata kakōn aitia ginetai.
sentences.l: So for many men their own designs become the causes of their troubles.
sentences.n: αἴτια here answers αἴτιον in the maids' reasoning above: they identified a cause correctly and then became one.
